errors.text: The proposed high-temperature boundary for strain-rate-insensitive yielding is opposite to the target: the target found negligible yield-strength sensitivity over 10^8-10^10 s^-1 at 10-600 K, whereas the hypothesis assigns it to temperatures above 0.7 Tm and diffusion-controlled deformation.

Diffusion-controlled creep, dislocation climb, and grain-boundary sliding generally introduce substantial time or strain-rate dependence; they do not justify the claim that the strain-rate sensitivity parameter approaches zero.
The hypothesis assumes a coarse-grained polycrystal and invokes grain-boundary sliding, while the target is a periodic single-crystal molecular-dynamics model with no grain boundaries.

The cited evidence primarily concerns quinary CoCrFeMnNi or unrelated precipitate-containing refractory alloys, not the quaternary equiatomic FeNiCrMn single crystal under the target simulation conditions.
